name: Neonatal Scleroderma

criteria.description: Presence of skin thickening and induration localized or generalized at birth or within the neonatal period
Skin biopsy showing dermal fibrosis with thickened collagen bundles and loss of adnexal structures
Detection of scleroderma-associated autoantibodies such as anti-topoisomerase I (Scl-70) or anti-centromere antibodies
Exclusion of infectious causes of skin induration and fibrosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of skin thickening with supportive histopathology findings; autoantibodies and exclusion of infection support diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; neonatal onset distinguishes from juvenile forms.

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) may be present
Normal or mildly elevated creatinine in renal involvement
imaging: Chest X-ray or CT showing interstitial lung changes in pulmonary fibrosis
MRI of affected limbs showing skin and subcutaneous tissue thickening
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; possible association with autoimmune predisposition
other: Skin biopsy demonstrating dermal fibrosis and loss of adnexal structures

distinguishingFeatures: Less extensive skin involvement at birth
Localized skin involvement without systemic features
Histopathology may overlap but clinical presentation differs

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin fibrosis with joint contractures
Signs of respiratory distress or pulmonary involvement
Evidence of renal crisis or hypertension
references: Miller FW, et al. Neonatal scleroderma: clinical features and pathogenesis. J Pediatr. 2020.
